rv.q: The Wedding Singer at the Metropolis is a non stop party.

Sheer exuberance and a fresh-faced cast fuel director Amber Mak’s breezy revival of this middling musical based on the 1998 film starring Adam Sandler as a wedding crooner and Drew Barrymore as the big-hearted waitress who catches his eye.
Ultimately, The Wedding Singer is like a perfectly curated ‘80s playlist: upbeat, a little cheesy, and impossible not to enjoy.
This is a fun show and the new staff just keeps getting stronger.

cn.t: Critics praise this energetic production for leaning hard into 1980s nostalgia with high-octane performances and neon-soaked charm, delivering a thoroughly entertaining and fun night of theater.
